argConstraint.description: A constraint on one call argument.

index.description: Zero-based argument index. Unique within a rule's args (a semantic check).

argPred.description: A stateless predicate over a single call argument (never a running total across calls), tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description: The argument must be the smart account's own address.
oneOf.title: is-self

address.description: The address (C- or G-address) the argument must equal.

values.description: The allowed string values (non-empty, no duplicates).

value.description: The exact u32 value the argument must equal.

doc-hash.description: Canonical doc_hash (64 lowercase hex) of the baseline document.

capConstraint.description: A cumulative spend cap over a rolling window. Lowers to OpenZeppelin's stateful `spending_limit` policy (perch itself is stateless).

limit.description: Maximum cumulative amount as a decimal string (a string, not a number, because an i128 amount does not fit a JSON number safely). Must parse as a POSITIVE i128 — positivity and the i128 range are semantic checks (outside this schema).

period-ledgers.description: Rolling-window length in ledgers. Must be non-zero.

token.description: Token contract (C-address) the cap is denominated in. Defaults to the rule's contract scope when omitted; cap/scope agreement is a cross-reference check (outside this schema).

circuitId.description: sha256 of the verifier's verification key (64 lowercase hex).

commitment.description: The credential's inner commitment (64 lowercase hex). That it encodes a CANONICAL BN254 field element (below the scalar modulus) is a semantic range check enforced by perch-ir's validator, outside this schema.

enrollmentId.description: 32 random bytes naming the enrolled credential (64 lowercase hex).

guardians.description: The guardian set: independent principals (not document signers). Non-empty, no duplicates.

principals.description: Who a rule authorizes, tagged by `type`.

signers.description: Declared signer ids, all of which must authorize. That each id is declared is a cross-reference check (outside this schema).

m.description: How many of `signers` must authorize (the M). Must be at least 1; the upper bound m <= N is a cross-reference check (outside this schema).

signers.description: Declared signer ids the quorum draws from (the N).

ack.description: Acknowledgement that this rule carries no signature check of its own. Must equal the sentinel verbatim or validation fails.

install-param-hex.description: Hex-encoded install parameter passed to the policy (may be empty).

quorum.description: How many guardians must authorize. At least 1; the upper bound quorum <= guardian count is a cross-reference check (outside this schema).

recoveryConfig.description: Opt-in account-recovery enrollment — who may recover this account and how. Reviewable configuration only, never the recovery attempt itself (see `docs/recovery/spec.md`).

baseline.description: Commitment to the baseline document compromise recovery restores. Omit to restrict the account to lost-key recovery.

delay-ledgers.description: Ledgers between an attempt becoming authorized and completable. Must be non-zero.

expiry-ledgers.description: Evidence/completion window and the furthest a reconfiguration or upgrade approval may reach. Must be non-zero.

max-cancels.description: Cap on evidence-based cancellations of authorized attempts. Must be non-zero.

profile.description: `loss`: the owner may reconfigure/remove recovery and cancel any attempt alone, keeping activity while an attempt is authorized. `protected`: reconfiguration/removal/upgrades also need the enrolled condition, and the account freezes while an attempt is authorized.

replaceable.description: Declared signer ids a recovery attempt may replace (non-empty, no duplicates). That each id is declared is a cross-reference check (outside this schema).

recoveryMode.description: How a recovery attempt is authorized, tagged by `type`. `combined` requires BOTH a valid proof and a guardian quorum against the same statement.

rule.description: A single policy rule: who (`principals`) may do what (`functions`, `args`) where (`scope`) until when (`not-after-ledger`), with an optional cumulative spend `cap`.

args.description: Constraints on call arguments, keyed by index. Omit for unconstrained; an explicit empty list or null is rejected. Argument-index uniqueness is a semantic check (outside this schema).

functions.description: Allowlist of function names. Omit the field for `all functions`; an explicit empty list is rejected as ambiguous, and an explicit null is rejected (it would silently authorize every function).

name.description: Human-readable rule name. Uniqueness and the compiler's byte-length cap are enforced outside this schema.

not-after-ledger.description: Ledger SEQUENCE (not a Unix timestamp) at or after which the rule stops authorizing. Must be non-zero; omit for no expiry.

scope.description: Where a rule applies, tagged by `type`.

address.description: The contract (C-address) the rule scopes to.

oneOf.description: Administrative operations on the smart account itself (signer/rule changes, upgrades).
oneOf.title: Self-admin scope

signerDecl.description: A declared signer: a document-local id plus how it authenticates. The method is discriminated by field shape, not a `type` tag — `verifier`+`key` is an external signer checked by a verifier contract, `address` is a CAP-0071 delegated address. A mixed or incomplete shape matches neither and fails closed.

id.description: Document-local id rules reference. Uniqueness is a semantic check (outside this schema).

key.description: Hex-encoded key material, opaque to perch. Decoded length must be 1..=MAX_SIGNER_KEY_LEN bytes (the pattern encodes that window and the even-length hex requirement).

verifier.description: Verifier contract (C-address) that checks this signer's signatures.

address.description: Delegate address (G… account or C… contract) the host authenticates via CAP-0071.

zkAdapter.description: The ZK adapter the controller calls (C-address).

zkPool.description: The membership pool whose roots proofs must use (C-address).

description: The reviewable artifact at the center of perch: a smart account's signers, rules, scopes, constraints, and optional recovery enrollment. This schema describes document format `version: 1` as perch-ir's strict parser (`from_json`) accepts it and its validator (`validate`) accepts the representable rules. Schema-valid is NOT the same as authorized or canonically encoded: duplicate raw keys, canonical (RFC 8785) encoding, cross-reference and semantic invariants, aggregate resource bounds, signatures, and authorization are all enforced elsewhere — see `docs/schema.md`.

network.description: Optional network identifier (a passphrase or short name). Omitted from the canonical form when absent; an explicit JSON null is rejected, so leave the key out rather than setting it null.

recovery.description: Optional account-recovery enrollment (reviewable configuration, never a recovery attempt). Omitted from the canonical form when absent, so a document that never enrolls recovery hashes exactly as before this field existed.

rules.description: The policy rules. Order is preserved and significant to the hash.

signers.description: Declared signers that rules reference by id. Per-document count and size caps (max signers, canonical bytes) are the compiler's aggregate bounds, not this schema's — see `docs/schema.md`.

version.description: Document format version. The only supported value is 1; perch-ir rejects anything else before looking at the rest of the document. A future wire format gets a new document version and a new schema (versioning policy: `docs/schema.md`).

title: Perch Policy Document
